newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-IRVINE AIMS TO CONSOLIDATE FERRARI PLACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-IRVINE AIMS TO CONSOLIDATE FERRARI PLACE.

text.p: As a teenager, Eddie Irvine would sneak into the Formula One paddock among the caravans and the sing-songs during outings to the British Grand Prix.
Now, at 31, Irvine knows he needs to sustain his improved form at this year's event if he is to retain his place alongside twice world champion Michael Schumacher in the Ferrari team next year.
Irvine's contract is up for renewal and Ferrari's option on his services expires at the end of the month.

"Of course, I want to stay at Ferrari," he said. "But I am not going to worry about it. I am happy here and I know that if I keep on doing the job to my best then I have a good chance. That's all there is to it -- and I'm not hunting around for anything else."
Rumours from Italy suggest Ferrari have been talking to Finland's Mika Salo as a possible replacement for the Briton, but none of these has been confirmed or substantiated.
This has left Irvine, whose consistency has helped Ferrari and Schumacher to the top of the constructors' and drivers' championships this year, waiting to see if his seat is safe.

"I don't think there is anyone out there, apart from Michael, who is better than me," he said. "In fact, I believe that had I been in a Williams this season I could have beaten Michael because, to be honest, I've always thought I was a better driver than either Jacques Villeneuve or Heinz-Harald Frentzen."
Irvine has four podium finishes to his name this year and they may prove to be decisive in the constructors championship at the end of the season if Williams sustain their challenge.

Second in Argentina, third at San Marino and Monaco and third in France, Irvine has been a vital support to a Ferrari team dedicated to helping German Schumacher to his third world championship triumph and the team's first drivers' title since 1979 and constructors' win since 1983.

Irvine, in his second season with the Italian giants, has come to terms with playing second fiddle for Ferrari and although he accepts his role as Schumacher's shadow, he has the utmost confidence in his own ability.

"The team is right behind Micheal and I am a bit of a sideshow," he said. "I don't get inferior equipment, but if there is something new then it's handed to Michael. I understand that because Michael is the one who is going to win the title this season. Why give it to me?"
He added: "Michael is up there alone and then a couple of guys are level behind him....and I'm one of them."
And he added that although he was sure his Italian critics were waiting for him to fall on his face, he remained a big admirer of the Italian supporters.
"I'm going to get a positive result, but, to be honest, if I'm on the podium at the British Grand Prix I don't think it would mean more than being on the podium at Imola, for instance.

"Imola is the home race for Ferrari, and I've got more support in Italy than in any country. But I still have a lot of feeling for going to race in Britain. After all I am British and I can remember all those old days when we drove up and down the country for the races.
"Brands Hatch used to be my favourite circuit in Britain but getting there was a bit of a nightmare in a clapped out old motorhome. That was before there were motorways, of course..."
This weekend, Irvine will be bidding to bury the critics with another excellent performance for Ferrari and a result that makes it impossible for them to replace him alongside Schumacher in 1998.
